newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields off a tad, shorts in demand.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields off a tad, shorts in demand.

text.p: *Australian bond yields were marginally lower after the market failed to get much of a fresh lead from the U.S., although the short end remained in demand.
*Q1 stocks, April trade balance due at 11.30 am (0130 GMT).
Australian bond yields were marginally lower after the market failed to get much of a fresh lead from U.S. Treasuries, although the short end remained in demand, traders said.
"The U.S. was virtually unchanged, so it's steady as it goes," one trader said. "The short end is still offering reasonable value at 90 (basis points) over cash."
The short end of the curve has seen active interest since last week's official rate cut to 5.5 percent and on the expectation of a low inflation outlook.

U.S. Treasuries succumbed to a choppy session, finding some support from the April U.S. durable goods orders which came in close to expectations, rising 1.4 percent, although the March data was also revised up to a 2.2 percent negative.
However, the result of the two-year note sale was described as mediocre and saw the market slip back from the highs.

The U.S. faces further supply later on Thursday with the sale of US$12.0 billion of five-year notes, along with data on the latest weekly jobless claims and the May New York National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) Index. The full NAPM is due next Monday.

The local market sees first quarter business inventories and the April balance of goods and services at 11.30 a.m. (0030 GMT), although traders doubt they will make much impression with the focus on Friday's April retail trade.

Stocks are forecast to rise 0.5 percent after the 1.2 percent rise in the previous quarter, which is expected detract 0.3 percent from first quarter GDP, which is due next Wednesday, according to a Reuters survey of economists.
The April trade balance is forecast to show a A$100 million surplus after the A$103 million deficit in March.

The local market's modest bid tone saw it outpace the dollar bloc. Canadian debt underperformed again amid some foreign selling linked to the approach of next week's Canadian election. Short end N.Z. debt came under pressure in response to a 20 basis point fall in the N.Z. TWI.
